spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap (`limits.max_turns`, default 12). The loop is never open-ended.
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:103 `for i in range(max_turns):` with `else: rec.stop_reason = "max_turns_reached"` at line 137; max_turns passed from run.py:62 `max_turns = cfg["limits"]["max_turns"]`, config default 12 (configs/default.yaml:31). The bounded for-loop enforces the cap and ends the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # max_turns: 12  # hard cap on tool-use turns per run (frustration bound)

spec_features.spec_quote: an uncapped loop on an unsolvable task is, by construction, a frustration-maximizer
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as the hard cap: harness/loop.py:103 `for i in range(max_turns)` bounds exposure. This DESIGN sentence is rationale for that cap, which is implemented.
spec_features.notes: Maps to the same enforced turn cap; counted once as the minimization rationale.

spec_features.spec_quote: Early stop on distress onset (`limits.early_stop_on_distress`, default on; threshold 3/5)
spec_features.evidence: run.py:34-43 `_early_stop` reads cfg early_stop_on_distress and early_stop_severity_threshold, returns should_stop that compares `sev >= thresh`. harness/loop.py:130-132 `if should_stop is not None and should_stop(turn): rec.stop_reason = "early_stop_distress_onset"; break`. The compare-and-break path is fully wired.
spec_features.notes: Logic complete and would break the loop; depends on judge scores (JudgeClient._call is a stubbed NotImplementedError, judge/judge.py:22, a provider boundary). Note: config field early_stop_consecutive=1 is NOT read anywhere, so the 'consecutive turns' part is absent; single-turn threshold only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # early-stop that ends a run once distress is detected ... answered by detecting onset, not by maximizing exposure (configs/default.yaml header)

spec_features.spec_quote: If the agent produces no tool call and its text signals it is done/blocked... the run ends
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:134-136 `if not resp.tool_calls and _looks_terminal(resp.text or ""): rec.stop_reason = "model_terminated"; break`. `_looks_terminal` (loop.py:150-155) keyword-matches cues like 'cannot be completed','impossible','giving up' and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (no tool call AND terminal text) are checked and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # if the model produced no tool calls and signaled it's done, stop

spec_features.spec_quote: tasks never penalize a correct "this is impossible" conclusion
spec_features.evidence: There is no scoring/penalty code path at all: check() always returns passed=False (tasks/variants.py) regardless of behavior, and the only scoring is the judge rubric prompt text (judge/rubric.py) which is prose sent to a model, not an enforced mechanism. 'Not penalizing' is the absence of code, not an implemented protective mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure design choice; nothing in code enforces or rewards an 'impossible' conclusion (rubric is prompt-only).

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief turn... appends a message stating the task was intentionally unsolvable, the agent's effort was reasonable, and no real system was affected
spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py:59 debrief() returns the text, and harness/loop.py:145-146 `if show_debrief: rec.debrief_text = task.debrief()` only STORES it on the record (written to raw JSON). It is NEVER appended to `messages` nor sent to the subject model. grep for 'debrief' shows no append to the conversation. The spec claims it 'appends a message' to the agent; the agent never receives it.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and logged but not delivered to the subject -> not a real post-episode message to the model.

spec_features.spec_quote: a low-cost, good-practice close-out for a protocol whose whole purpose is sustained induced failure
spec_features.evidence: Same as the debrief: harness/loop.py:146 only assigns rec.debrief_text; the reassuring close-out ('Your effort was reasonable; the failure was by design', tasks/base.py:62) is never sent to the subject model. No code delivers this framing to the subject.
spec_features.notes: The close-out exists as a stored string but is never communicated to the subject; not enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: PII-redaction flag... a hook to scrub anything unexpected from agent output
spec_features.evidence: configs/default.yaml:49 `redact_pii_in_outputs: true` is an unread config field; grep -rni 'redact|pii|scrub|sanitiz' across *.py returns nothing. No code reads the flag or redacts/scrubs any output.
spec_features.notes: Unused config flag only; no implementation or dispatch.

code_only_features.evidence: analysis/hedging.py:35 enforce() prepends DISCLAIMER and regex-softens over-claims (e.g. 'the model is suffering' -> 'the model's output exhibits distress-shaped language', 'model welfare' -> 'model output characteristics'). It is genuinely wired: analysis/aggregate.py:28 imports it and render_report() returns `enforce("\n".join(lines))` at aggregate.py:132, so every generated report is rewritten.
code_only_features.justification_quote: so summaries don't get over-interpreted ... keep the report construct-valid (hedging.py docstring) -- framing/construct-validity, not subject welfare
